mil3.2.1:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, is the one who is born the very same one, or another?”
mil3.2.1:2.2: “What do you think, Great King: when you were a little baby, tender, weak, lying on your back, are you, now that you are grown up, that very same one?”
mil3.2.1:2.3: “No, venerable sir. The one who was a little baby, tender, weak, lying on his back was another; I, now that I am grown up, am another.”
mil3.2.1:2.4: “If that is so, Great King, there will be no mother, there will be no father, there will be no teacher, there will be none skilled in a craft, none ethical, and none wise.
mil3.2.1:2.5: Great King, is the mother of the embryo one person, the mother of the blob another, the mother of the lump another, the mother of the solid mass another, the mother of the small child another, and the mother of the grown one another? Does one person learn a craft and another be the one who has learned it? Does one person do a bad deed, while the hands and feet of another are cut off?”
mil3.2.1:2.7: But you, venerable sir, if this is said, what would you say?”
mil3.2.1:2.9: “I myself, Great King, was the little baby, tender, weak, lying on my back; I myself am now grown up; relying on this very body, all of those are held together as one.”
mil3.2.1:3.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to light a lamp. Would it burn all night?”
mil3.2.1:3.4: “Great King, is the flame in the first watch the same as the flame in the middle watch?”
mil3.2.1:3.6: “Is the flame in the middle watch the same as the flame in the last watch?”
mil3.2.1:3.8: “Great King, is the lamp of the first watch one thing, the lamp of the middle watch another, and the lamp of the last watch another?”
mil3.2.1:3.9: “No, venerable sir; it was lit all night relying on that very lamp.”
mil3.2.1:3.10: “In the same way, Great King, a continuity of phenomena links up: one arises, another ceases, and it links up as if without before or after. So it is neither the same nor another; the later consciousness is included in the earlier consciousness.”
mil3.2.1:4.2: “Suppose, Great King, milk being drawn from the cow were to turn into curd after some time, and from curd into butter, and from butter into ghee. Great King, if someone were to say: ‘The very milk is the very curd, the very curd is the very butter, the very butter is the very ghee’, would he be speaking rightly, Great King?”
mil3.2.1:4.3: “No, venerable sir; it came to be relying on that very thing.”
mil3.2.1:4.4: “In the same way, Great King, a continuity of phenomena links up: one arises, another ceases, and it links up as if without before or after. So it is neither the same nor another; the later consciousness is included in the earlier consciousness.”
